Continued from page 1 of the consultation of 05/09/2025.
The patient reports persistent low back pain, rated 7 out of 10.
He confirms adherence to the prescribed physical therapy and medication schedule.
Discussion focused on the efficacy of conservative measures and the need for further intervention.
We reviewed the risks and benefits of an epidural steroid injection.
Plan: left L4-L5 transforaminal epidural steroid injection.
We also discussed continuing physical therapy and managing pain with prescribed medications.
Restrictions: sedentary duty, no lifting over 15 pounds, until re-evaluation on 06/20/2025.
The patient understands the limitations of the current treatment phase.
In my opinion the L4-L5 disc protrusion is causally related to the lifting injury of 03/11/2025 described by the patient, within a reasonable degree of medical probability.
The patient has not reached maximum medical improvement.
Follow up is scheduled for the re-evaluation date to assess the efficacy of the intervention.
Neurological findings as documented on page 1.
The patient remains motivated to return to work safely.
